claims.text: Conventional high-purity ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared ZrB2 typically exhibits notable porosity and microstructural defects.
Adding a small, optimized amount of B4C to ZrB2 enables transient liquid-phase sintering.
B4C addition can lower the ZrB2 densification temperature from above 2300 °C to around 2000 °C.
The B4C additive forms a transient liquid at ZrB2 particle boundaries during sintering.
The transient liquid enhances particle rearrangement and interparticle contact.
The transient liquid promotes mass transport during sintering.
Transient liquid-phase sintering facilitates healing of interparticle voids.
B4C-assisted transient liquid-phase sintering reduces residual porosity in ZrB2.
Residual pores and related defects act as initiation sites for failure in a corrosive liquid-plating environment.
B4C-modified ZrB2 sintered around 2000 °C will have mechanical integrity comparable to or better than conventional ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
B4C-modified ZrB2 will develop fewer pores or holes during long-duration liquid-plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The pores or holes formed in B4C-modified ZrB2 after plating-bath exposure will be smaller than those in conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Conventional ZrB2 has a greater propensity for defect formation under prolonged liquid-plating conditions.
